hello.note: Reply: yauwa, sannu. Also very common: salamu alaikum (reply: wa alaikumus salam).

goodbye.note: Literally 'until a while'. For a longer parting: sai wani lokaci (until another time).

please.note: Literally 'for God's sake', but it is simply the everyday polite 'please'.

thank_you.note: Na gode sosai: thank you very much.

youre_welcome.note: Literally 'it's nothing'. Also common: babu damuwa (no worries).

yes.note: Also written i. When someone calls your name, answer na'am.

no.note: The ' is a catch in the throat, as in English uh-oh.

sorry.note: To a woman: ki yi haƙuri. Sannu shows sympathy (someone is hurt or tired); it is not an apology.

excuse_me.note: Add malam to a man or malama to a woman: gafara dai, malam.

good_morning.note: Literally 'how did you sleep?'. Reply: lafiya lau. Also common: barka da safiya.

how_are_you.note: To a woman: yaya kike? Also very common: ina lafiya? (reply: lafiya lau).

nice_to_meet_you.text: Na ji daɗin haɗuwa da kai
nice_to_meet_you.note: To a woman: na ji daɗin haɗuwa da ke.

where_from.note: To a woman: daga ina kike?

im_from.note: Also: na fito daga … (I come from …).

speak_english.note: To a woman: kina jin Turanci? Hausa 'hears' (ji) a language rather than 'speaks' it.

speak_slowly.text: Don Allah, ka yi magana a hankali
speak_slowly.note: To a woman: don Allah, ki yi magana a hankali.

where.note: Example: ina kasuwa? (where is the market?)

what.note: Short form: me?, as in me ka ce? (what did you say?)

who.note: Short form: wa? Asking about a woman: wace ce?

can_you_help.text: Don Allah, za ka iya taimaka mini?
can_you_help.note: To a woman: don Allah, za ki iya taimaka mini?

what_time.note: Answer like: ƙarfe uku ne (it's three o'clock).

one.note: ɗ is an implosive d, said with a little inward gulp of air.

water.note: Drinking water: ruwan sha. Ruwa also means rain.

bread.note: Gurasa is a traditional Hausa bread.

menu_please.text: Don Allah, kawo mini jerin abinci
menu_please.note: In small eateries people simply ask: me kuke da shi? (what do you have?)

bill_please.note: Literally 'how much is the money?', the usual way to settle up after eating.

delicious.note: Also common: akwai daɗi! or ya yi daɗi!

enjoy_meal.note: Literally 'in the name of God'; said to invite others to start eating.

right.note: Turn right: juya dama. Dama also means 'chance'.

stop_here.note: Also common: sauke ni nan (drop me here).

train_station.note: Jirgin ƙasa means train; tasha is any station or bus park.

is_it_far.note: Also: yana da nisa? Common answer: ba nisa (it's not far).

too_expensive.note: To bargain: rage mini (bring the price down for me).

small.note: With a feminine noun: ƙarama. Plural: ƙanana.

later.note: Later today. For 'later on, afterwards': daga baya.

good_evening.note: Also: ina wuni? (how was your day?), answered lafiya lau.

good_night.note: Also: mu kwana lafiya (let us sleep well).

every_day.note: Also: kowace rana (each day). Kullum can also mean 'always'.

help.note: Also: ku taimake ni! (help me, all of you!)

call_police.note: 'y is a glottalised y, said with a catch in the throat.

dont_feel_well.note: Also: ba ni da lafiya (I'm unwell).

allergic.note: Hausa has no everyday word for allergy; this says 'my body does not get along with …'.

be_careful.note: To a woman: ki yi hankali! Quick warning to anyone: a hankali!

i_like_it.note: If 'it' is a feminine noun: ina sonta.

dont_like_it.note: If 'it' is a feminine noun: ba na sonta.

im_tired.note: A common greeting is ina gajiya? (how's the tiredness?), answered ba gajiya.

welcome.note: Also: barka da zuwa! or maraba!

congratulations.note: To a woman: ina taya ki murna! Also: madalla! (well done!)

my_family.note: Iyali usually means your wife and children; for relatives in general say dangina.

mother.note: Your mother, politely: mahaifiyarka; uwarka on its own can sound like an insult. Children say Mama or Inna.

father.note: Your father, politely: mahaifinka; ubanka on its own can sound like an insult. Children say Baba.

brother.note: Older brother: yaya; younger brother: ƙane. Ɗan'uwa can also mean any close relative.

sister.note: Older sister: yaya; younger sister: ƙanwa.

child.note: Daughter: 'ya. Children: 'ya'ya. A kid in general is yaro.

friend.note: Female friend: abokiya. Between women, a friend is ƙawa.

this_is_my_friend.note: For a female friend: wannan abokiyata ce (between women: wannan ƙawata ce).

are_you_married.note: To a woman: kina da aure? Answer: ina da aure (I'm married).

monday.note: On Monday: ranar Litinin. The same pattern works for every day.

friday.note: Also the name of the Friday congregational prayer.

weekend.note: Literally 'end of the week'. Many people also say sati for week.

what_day.note: Answer like: yau Juma'a ce (today is Friday).

next_week.note: Also: sati mai zuwa. Last week: makon da ya wuce.

eleven.note: In 11–19, sha joins ten and the unit: goma sha biyu, goma sha uku…

twenty.note: Tens and units are joined by da: ashirin da ɗaya (21).

years_old.note: Example: ina da shekara talatin (I'm thirty). Also: shekaruna … (my years are …).

red.note: Same with feminine nouns. Plural: jajaye.

yellow.note: Also: ruwan ɗorawa, named after the yellow pulp of the locust bean.

what_colour.note: Launi means colour; kala is also very common.

that_one.note: With a feminine noun: waccan. Plural: waɗancan.

another_one.note: Literally 'add one for me'. Also: wani ɗaya, don Allah.

its_hot.note: Also: akwai zafi. Very hot: ana zafi sosai.

its_raining.note: Also: ana ruwan sama (sama is the sky).

its_sunny.note: Literally 'the sun has come out'. Rana means both sun and day.

its_windy.note: Iska also means air. Strong wind: iska mai ƙarfi.

weather_today.note: Yanayi is the weather word used in forecasts.

beautiful_day.note: Gari (town) also means the weather around you: gari ya yi sanyi (it has turned cold).

summer.note: The hot season before the rains, about March to May. Rainy season: damina.

winter.note: The cool, dry harmattan season, about December to February.

have_reservation.note: Literally 'a room has been kept for me'. Many people simply say: na yi booking.

room.note: My room: ɗakina. Room number: lambar ɗaki.

luggage.note: Means belongings in general. My luggage: kayana.

wifi_password.note: Most people just say password: mene ne password ɗin Wi-Fi?

check_out_time.text: Ƙarfe nawa ya kamata in bar ɗakin?
check_out_time.note: Literally 'at what time should I leave the room?'. Hotel staff often just say check-out.

next_train.text: Yaushe jirgin ƙasa na gaba zai tashi?

is_this_seat_free.note: Literally 'is there someone here?'. Also: zan iya zama a nan? (may I sit here?)

what_do_you_do.note: To a woman: wane aiki kike yi?

i_work_in.note: Example: ina aiki a banki (I work in a bank).

im_student.note: A woman says: ni ɗaliba ce.

meeting.note: At work many people also say mitin.

im_busy.note: Literally 'I have work'. Also: ba ni da lokaci (I have no time).

day_off.note: Hutu means rest or a holiday.

lets_start.note: Many people add bismillah first: bismillah, mu fara.

good_job.note: To a woman: kin yi ƙoƙari! Also: madalla! or da kyau!

table_for_two.text: Don Allah, tebur na mutum biyu

what_recommend.text: Me ya fi daɗi a nan?
what_recommend.note: Literally 'what is tastiest here?', the usual way to ask for a tip.

not_spicy.text: Don Allah, kada a sa yaji
not_spicy.note: Yaji is hot pepper spice. Just a little: yaji kaɗan.

vegetarian_food.note: Literally 'food without meat'. About yourself: ba na cin nama (I don't eat meat).

more_water.note: Ƙara mini works for more of anything: ƙara mini shayi.

no_sugar.text: Don Allah, kada a sa sukari

im_full.note: People often add alhamdulillah (praise be to God) after a meal.

takeaway.text: Zan tafi da shi, don Allah
takeaway.note: Literally 'I'll leave with it'. Also: a zuba mini a leda (put it in a bag for me).

it_was_delicious.note: To stress it: ya yi daɗi sosai (it was really delicious).

keep_change.note: To a woman: ki riƙe canjin. Also simply: bar shi (leave it).

head.note: Kai also means 'you' (to a man) and 'hey!'.

stomach.note: Ciki also means 'inside'. Stomach ache: ciwon ciki.

head_hurts.note: Also: ina ciwon kai (I have a headache).

have_fever.note: Malaria is often called zazzaɓin cizon sauro (fever from mosquito bites).

medicine.note: Also means a cure or remedy, traditional ones included.

dentist.note: Haƙori means tooth. Toothache: ciwon haƙori.

need_rest.note: Also: ina so in ɗan huta (I'd like to rest a little).

feel_better.note: Asked ya jiki? (how are you feeling?), people reply da sauƙi (better).

get_well.note: Said to anyone who is ill. Also: Allah ya ba ka lafiya! (to a woman: ba ki).

lets_meet.note: Example: mu haɗu gobe (let's meet tomorrow).

are_you_free.note: To a woman: kina da lokaci gobe?

call_me.note: To a woman: don Allah, ki kira ni. Also common: ka buga mini waya.

your_number.text: Don Allah, mene ne lambar wayarka?
your_number.note: To a woman: don Allah, mene ne lambar wayarki?

see_you_soon.text: Sai nan ba da jimawa ba
see_you_soon.note: For later the same day, sai anjima is usual.

have_nice_day.note: Said when parting during the day. In the evening: a kwana lafiya.

good_luck.note: Sa'a means luck. Also: Allah ya taimaka!

happy_birthday.note: Often followed by: Allah ya ƙara shekaru masu albarka (may God add blessed years).

thanks_a_lot.note: Also: na gode ƙwarai. A warm extra: Allah ya saka da alheri (God reward you).

miss_you.note: To a woman: ina kewarki. On meeting again: na yi kewarka (I've missed you).
